p.src: When Baochai heard Qiuwen say that Xiren was unwell, she hurried in to see her. Qiaojie and Ping'er followed her to Xiren's kang. They found Xiren racked by unbearable pain in her heart; presently she fainted. Baochai and the others revived her by giving her hot water, helped her lie down again, and sent for a physician. Qiaojie asked Baochai, “How did Sister Xiren become so ill?” Baochai replied, “The night before last, she grieved herself sick with weeping, grew faint, and collapsed. Madam had someone help her back here, and she took to her bed. There was trouble outside, so no physician was called to examine her, and that is why she has come to this.” As she spoke, the physician arrived, and Baochai and the others withdrew a little. After taking her pulse, the physician said that her illness had been caused by sudden anger and distress; he wrote a prescription and left. As it happened, Xiren had dimly heard that if Baoyu did not return, everyone in his rooms would be dismissed; the shock had made her still worse. After the physician had examined her, Qiuwen decocted the medicine for her. Lying there alone, still dazed and unsettled, she seemed to see Baoyu before her; then, in a haze, he seemed to be a monk holding a register and turning its pages as he said, “Do not delude yourself. I no longer know any of you.” Xiren seemed about to speak to him when Qiuwen came in and said, “The medicine is ready, Sister. Please take it.” Xiren opened her eyes, realized it had been a dream, and told no one about it. After taking the medicine, she pondered carefully to herself: “Baoyu must have gone away with the monk. The last time he tried to take the jade outside, he already looked as though he meant to make his escape. I caught hold of him, but instead of teasing, pushing, and fondling me as he usually did, he showed me not the least affection. Later he became even more weary of Second Mistress. Nor did he show the slightest affection before any of the other young ladies. That is what it looks like when someone attains enlightenment. But even if you attained enlightenment, how could you abandon Second Mistress! Madam assigned me to attend you. Though my monthly allowance was fixed at that rank, I was never formally acknowledged before Master and Madam as one of your concubines. If Master and Madam send me away, people will laugh at me if I stubbornly refuse to leave; yet if I do leave, I cannot bear it when I remember Baoyu's affection for me.” Whichever way she turned the matter over, she found herself in an impossible predicament. Remembering how the dream had seemed to tell her that he and she were not destined for each other, she thought, “I would be better off dead and done with it.” Yet after taking the medicine, the pain in her heart diminished considerably; unable to remain in bed, she could only force herself to carry on. After a few days, she rose and resumed attending Baochai. Baochai missed Baoyu, shed tears in secret, and lamented her unhappy fate. She also knew that her mother was making costly and complicated arrangements to redeem her brother from punishment, so she could not help lending her own thought to the matter. But we shall leave this aside for now.

p.src: Meanwhile, Jia Zheng escorted Grandmother Jia's coffin, while Jia Rong conveyed the coffins of Qin-shi, Xifeng, and Yuanyang. Upon reaching Jinling, they first laid them to rest. Jia Rong also personally escorted Daiyu's remains to their burial place. Jia Zheng attended to the affairs of the family burial ground. One day a letter arrived from home. Reading it line by line, he came to the news that Baoyu and Jia Lan had passed the examination, and naturally rejoiced. But when he read farther and learned that Baoyu had disappeared, he grew troubled again and had no choice but to hurry home. On the journey he heard that an imperial amnesty had been proclaimed, and another letter from home confirmed that he had indeed been pardoned and restored to office. p.src: One day, when they reached the vicinity of Piling Post Station, the weather suddenly turned cold and snow began to fall, so they moored in a quiet place. Jia Zheng sent his attendants ashore to deliver calling cards and decline his friends' invitations, saying in every case that the boat would depart at once and that he dared not trouble them. p.src: Listening as he ran after them, Jia Zheng rounded a small rise, and suddenly they vanished. By then he was faint and panting from the chase, filled with alarm and uncertainty. Looking back, he saw that his own page had also come running after him. Jia Zheng asked, “Did you see those three men just now?” The page replied, “Yes, I did. I saw Master giving chase, and so I followed after you. But afterward I could see only Master; the three men were gone.” Jia Zheng wanted to go farther, but before him lay only a vast, snow-white wilderness without a soul in sight. Knowing that something uncanny had occurred, Jia Zheng had no choice but to turn back.

p.src: When the servants returned to the boat and found Jia Zheng absent from the cabin, they questioned the boatmen, who said, “His lordship went ashore in pursuit of two monks and a Taoist.” They followed the tracks through the snow to meet him and, seeing Jia Zheng approaching in the distance, hurried forward to receive him and returned to the boat together. Jia Zheng sat down, and only after catching his breath did he recount how he had seen Baoyu. The servants made their report and proposed searching for him in that vicinity. Jia Zheng sighed. “You do not understand. I saw this with my own eyes; it was no ghostly apparition. Moreover, the song I heard was profoundly mysterious. Baoyu was born with a piece of jade in his mouth, which was strange in itself. I knew from the first that it was an ill omen, but the Old Lady doted on him, and so we raised him to this day. As for that monk and Taoist, I too have seen them three times. The first was when they came to speak of the jade’s virtues. The second was when Baoyu lay gravely ill: they took the jade and chanted over it, whereupon he recovered. The third was when they brought the jade back and sat in the front hall; the instant I turned my head, they vanished. I found it rather extraordinary, but supposed that Baoyu was truly blessed and that holy monks and immortal Taoists had come to protect him. Little did I know that Baoyu had descended to the mortal world to undergo his destined tribulations, and had kept the Old Lady deceived for nineteen years! Only now have I been made to understand.” At this point, tears fell from his eyes. The servants said, “If Second Master Baoyu truly was a monk descended to the mortal world, he ought never to have passed the provincial examination. Why did he leave only after he had passed?” Jia Zheng replied, “What could you know of it? Stars in heaven, aged monks in the mountains, and spirits dwelling in caves—all have temperaments of their own. You know how Baoyu never willingly applied himself to books, yet whenever he gave the least attention to anything, there was nothing he could not master. That peculiar disposition of his was unlike anyone else’s.” As he spoke, he sighed several more times. The others tried to console him by speaking of Brother Lan’s success and the revival of the family fortunes. Jia Zheng resumed writing his letter home, included an account of this event, and urged the whole family not to grieve for Baoyu. When he had finished and sealed it, he immediately sent a servant home with it. Jia Zheng himself followed soon afterward. But we shall leave this for the present.

p.src: Now, when Aunt Xue received word that the offense had been pardoned, she sent Xue Ke around to borrow money wherever he could. She also gathered what she could herself until the redemption payment was complete. The Board of Punishments approved the settlement and accepted the silver, and upon receipt of a brief official document Xue Pan was released. There is no need to describe in detail the reunion of mother and son, sisters and brothers; naturally, joy and sorrow mingled. Xue Pan swore, “If I ever relapse into my old ways, may I be murdered and hacked to pieces!” Seeing him speak so, Aunt Xue reached to cover his mouth. “It is enough that you firmly resolve to reform. Must you still let your tongue run wild and swear such bloody, dreadful oaths? Think how much Xiangling has suffered since she came to you. Your wife has already brought about her own death. Though we are poor now, we still have enough for another mouth. My thought is to acknowledge Xiangling as your proper wife. What do you say?” Xue Pan nodded his willing assent. Baochai and the others also said, “That is precisely what ought to be done.” This flustered Xiangling so much that her face turned scarlet. “I can serve the master just as I have always done. Why is any of this necessary?” she said. Everyone at once began addressing her as the young mistress of the household, and not one of them objected. Xue Pan wished to go and thank the Jia family, and Aunt Xue and Baochai came with him. After meeting the others, they sat together and exchanged many words. While they were talking, Jia Zheng’s servant happened to arrive home that very day. He presented the letter and announced, “His lordship will be here within a few days.” Lady Wang asked Jia Lan to read the letter aloud to her. When Jia Lan reached the passage in which Jia Zheng described seeing Baoyu with his own eyes, everyone burst into bitter weeping; Lady Wang, Baochai, Xiren, and the others wept most grievously of all. They then spent some time explaining Jia Zheng’s words in the letter that the family “need not grieve, for he had only borrowed a mortal womb.” “Rather than have him become an official only to meet with ill fortune, commit some offense, and ruin the family and its property, surely this is better. Better that our family should produce a Buddha. It was because the master and mistress had accumulated virtue that he came to be born into our household. Not to speak irreverently of the past, even the old master of the eastern mansion practiced spiritual disciplines for more than ten years without attaining immortality. To attain Buddhahood is harder still. If you look at it this way, madam, your heart will find relief.” Weeping, Lady Wang said to Aunt Xue, “Baoyu abandoned me, and for that I still resent him. But what I lament is my daughter-in-law’s cruel fate. They had been married only a year or two—how could he harden his heart, cast everything aside, and leave?” Aunt Xue was deeply grieved to hear this. Baochai wept until she lost consciousness. All the men were outside, and Lady Wang said, “I spent my whole life fearing what might happen to him. He had only just married and passed the provincial examination, and when I learned that his wife was with child, I had at last begun to feel some joy. I never dreamed it would end like this!

p.src: Had I known it would come to this, I should never have arranged the marriage and blighted another family’s daughter!” Aunt Xue said, “This was ordained for her. What else can families such as ours say about it? Fortunately she is with child. If she bears a grandson in due course, he will surely make something of himself, and in the end her life will have borne fruit. Look at the young widow Li Wan: now that Brother Lan has passed the provincial examination and may become a Presented Scholar next year, will he not then take office? She has already endured her full measure of bitterness, and the sweetness she enjoys now is also the reward of her goodness. You know your niece’s nature, sister. She is neither harsh nor frivolous, so you need not worry.” Lady Wang found Aunt Xue’s words eminently reasonable and thought, “Even as a child, Baochai was exceptionally modest and serene, free from worldly desires, and exceedingly fond of simplicity. That must be why this has befallen her. Truly, every human life has its appointed fate. Though she is weeping bitterly, she has not lost one whit of her composure and dignity; instead, she even tries to comfort me. That is truly remarkable! Who would have thought that a person like Baoyu should have not the least share of blessing in this mortal world!” After reflecting for a while, she felt considerably more reconciled. Then her thoughts turned to Xiren. “As for the other maids, there is no real difficulty: the older ones can be married off, while the younger ones can serve the Second Young Mistress. But what is to be done with Xiren alone?” There were too many people present to discuss it then, so she decided to wait until evening and consult Aunt Xue.

p.src: That day Aunt Xue did not return home, for fear that Baochai would weep bitterly, but remained in Baochai's room to comfort her. Baochai, however, was exceedingly sensible. After reflecting on all that had happened, she thought, “Baoyu was always an extraordinary person. The causes laid down in former lives have their appointed course, so there is no reason to blame Heaven or other people.” She then explained these higher principles to her mother. Aunt Xue's mind was set at ease instead, and she went to Lady Wang and first repeated what Baochai had said. Lady Wang nodded and sighed. “If I were without virtue, I would not deserve such a fine daughter-in-law.” As she spoke, grief overcame her once more. Aunt Xue comforted her for a while longer, then brought up Xiren. “I have seen how terribly thin Xiren has grown lately. Her whole heart is fixed on young Master Bao. A lawful wife is naturally bound to remain faithful, and there are concubines who choose to do the same. But though Xiren was counted among his chamber women, her relationship with young Master Bao was never formally acknowledged.” Lady Wang said, “I was just thinking about that and meant to wait until I could discuss it with you. If we send her away, I fear she will refuse and try to take her own life; yet even if we let her stay, I fear the master will not consent. That is what makes it so difficult.” Aunt Xue said, “I am certain your husband will never allow her to remain faithful to Baoyu. Besides, he knows nothing about Xiren's circumstances and surely thinks of her as no more than a maid. What reason could there be to keep her? You need only summon her own family and firmly instruct them to arrange a respectable marriage for her, while giving her a generous dowry. She is a good-hearted child and still young. Then the time she spent serving you will not have been in vain, and it will show that you have treated her generously. As for Xiren, I shall have to reason with her carefully. Even when her family is summoned, there is no need to tell her. We should wait until they have truly settled upon a good family, then make our own inquiries. If the household is indeed comfortably provided for and the prospective husband is a decent-looking fellow, only then shall we send her away.” Lady Wang replied, “That is an excellent plan. Otherwise, if the master handled it rashly, would I not have ruined yet another person's life?” Aunt Xue nodded. “Indeed you would!” After exchanging a few more words, she took leave of Lady Wang and returned to Baochai's room.

You need only summon her own family and firmly instruct them to arrange a respectable marriage for her, while giving her a generous dowry.
She is a good-hearted child and still young. Then the time she spent serving you will not have been in vain, and it will show that you have treated her generously.
As for Xiren, I shall have to reason with her carefully.

Even when her family is summoned, there is no need to tell her. We should wait until they have truly settled upon a good family, then make our own inquiries. If the household is indeed comfortably provided for and the prospective husband is a decent-looking fellow, only then shall we send her away.”
Lady Wang replied, “That is an excellent plan.

Aunt Xue nodded. “Indeed you would!”
After exchanging a few more words, she took leave of Lady Wang and returned to Baochai's room.

p.src: Seeing Xiren's face covered with traces of tears, Aunt Xue spent some time consoling her and reasoning with her by means of examples. Xiren was honest by nature and no glib talker. To each thing Aunt Xue said, she gave an answer, and at last replied, “I am only a servant. Your Ladyship thinks enough of me to say these things, and I have never dared disobey my mistress.” Hearing her words, Aunt Xue thought, “What a gentle and obedient child!” She grew even fonder of her. Baochai then repeated her discourse on the higher principles of duty, and everyone regained a measure of peace.

I beg Your Excellencies to instruct me how I should express my thanks.” The courtiers said that they would memorialize the throne on his behalf and request the Emperor's pleasure. His Majesty declared the matter remarkable and pronounced that Baoyu's essays were indeed pure and extraordinary, and that he must surely have passed through the cycle before, which explained why he was as he was. p.src: On returning home, Jia Zheng was received by Jia Lian and Jia Zhen. He recounted what had been said at court, to everyone's delight. Jia Zhen then reported, “The Ningguo mansion has been completely put in order. Once we have formally reported the matter, we intend to move back there. Longcui Nunnery has been enclosed within the garden and set aside for Fourth Sister's quiet convalescence.” Jia Zheng said nothing. After some time, however, he delivered a lengthy injunction that they must look up to Heaven and repay the imperial favor. Jia Lian took the opportunity to report, “As for Qiaojie's marriage, Father and Mother are both willing to give her to the Zhou family as their daughter-in-law.” Jia Zheng had learned the whole story of Qiaojie the previous night and replied, “Let your father and mother decide the matter. Never mind that they live in the country. So long as the family is respectable and the young man is willing to study and better himself, that is enough. Surely not every official at court was born in the city?” Jia Lian answered, “Yes,” and continued, “Father is growing old and has a chronic phlegmatic ailment. If he spends several years quietly recuperating, all our affairs will naturally depend upon you, Second Master.” Jia Zheng said, “The thought of living quietly in the country accords very well with my own wishes. It is only that the favor I have received is so profound, and I have yet to repay it.” Having said this, Jia Zheng went into the inner apartments. Jia Lian sent for Grannie Liu, who came and agreed to the match. When Grannie Liu met Lady Wang and the others, she spoke of how the family would rise to high office in the future, rebuild its fortunes, and flourish through generations of descendants. While she was speaking, a maid announced, “Hua Zifang's wife has come to pay her respects.” Lady Wang asked her a few questions. Hua Zifang's wife explained that a relative had acted as matchmaker and proposed a family named Jiang in the southern part of the city. They owned a house, land, and a shop; the prospective husband was a few years older but had never married, and was exceptionally handsome besides. Lady Wang was pleased and said, “Go and accept the proposal. Come back in a few days to fetch your sister.” Lady Wang also sent people to make inquiries, and everyone spoke well of the family. Lady Wang then informed Baochai and invited Aunt Xue to explain the matter carefully to Xiren. Xiren was overwhelmed with grief, yet dared not disobey. She remembered how Baoyu had visited her home years before and, upon returning, had declared that he would never send her back even if he died. “Now Her Ladyship is determined to impose her will. If I say I will remain here, people will call me shameless; but if I leave, it will truly be against my heart.” She wept until her throat choked and no sound would come. After Aunt Xue, Baochai, and the others earnestly tried to console her, her thoughts took another turn: “If I die here, I shall only spoil Her Ladyship's kind intentions. I ought to die in my own home instead.” And so, suppressing her grief, Xiren kowtowed and took leave of everyone. What passed when the sisters parted was naturally too painful to tell. Resolved to die, Xiren boarded the carriage and returned home. When she saw her brother and sister-in-law, she could only weep and was unable to utter a word.

p.src: Hua Zifang showed her all the betrothal gifts sent by the Jiang family, then pointed out each item of the trousseau he had prepared for her, explaining which things had been bestowed by Lady Wang and which he had purchased himself. p.src: At last the auspicious wedding day arrived. Xiren was not a bold, headstrong woman, so she meekly submitted to her distress and entered the bridal sedan, thinking she would decide what to do once she reached the Jiang home. Yet after entering the household, she found that the Jiang family had arranged everything with the utmost care and had followed in every respect the rites due to a principal wife. The moment she entered, all the maids and serving women addressed her as mistress of the house. Xiren now wanted to die there, but feared that she would harm the family and repay all their kindness with ingratitude. That night she wept and refused to yield, but her bridegroom treated her with the greatest tenderness and patiently accommodated her every wish. When the trunks were opened the next day, the bridegroom saw a bright scarlet sash and realized that she had been Baoyu's maid. Until then he had known only that his bride had served the Lady Dowager; it had never occurred to him that she might be Xiren. Remembering Baoyu's former kindness to him, Jiang Yuhan was filled with uneasiness and shame and treated Xiren with even greater consideration. He then deliberately brought out the pale pine-flower-green sash he had exchanged with Baoyu. When Xiren saw it, she learned that this man named Jiang was none other than Jiang Yuhan and began to believe that marriages were indeed predestined. Only then did Xiren reveal what was in her heart. Jiang Yuhan sighed deeply and admired her fidelity; he dared not force her and treated her with still greater tenderness and understanding, until Xiren truly found there was nowhere left for her to die. p.src: We shall say no more of the new life that now opened before Xiren. Let us instead tell how Jia Yucun was charged with extortion and corruption. The case was tried and he was convicted, but when a general amnesty was proclaimed, he was merely stripped of his official status and reduced to a commoner. Yucun sent his family ahead, while he himself set out with a young servant and a cartload of luggage, arriving at the Ferry of Awakening by the Ford of Rushing Waters. There he saw a Taoist emerge from a thatched shelter by the ferry and come forward to clasp his hands in greeting. Yucun recognized Zhen Shiyin and promptly bowed in return. Shiyin said, “I trust you have been well since we parted, Mr. Jia?” Yucun replied, “So the venerable immortal truly is Mr. Zhen! Why, when we met before, did you fail to acknowledge me even though we stood face to face? Later, when I learned that the thatched pavilion had burned down, I was deeply alarmed. Now that fortune has allowed us to meet again, I admire still more the profundity of your virtue and attainment. Alas, in my base stupidity I remained incorrigible, and so have come to my present state.” Zhen Shiyin said, “At that time Your Excellency held high office and noble rank. How would this poor Taoist have dared claim your acquaintance? Only because we were old friends did I venture to offer you a few words of counsel, never expecting Your Excellency to cast them so utterly aside. p.src: Yucun gladly accepted the invitation, and the two walked off hand in hand while the servant drove the carriage behind them, until they reached a thatched hermitage. Shiyin ushered Yucun inside and invited him to sit, whereupon a young attendant served them tea. Yucun then asked the immortal master how he had transcended the world of dust. Shiyin smiled. “In the space of a single thought, the mortal world is utterly transformed. You have come from the midst of splendor and prosperity; surely you know that in that land of wealth and tender delights there was a Baoyu—a Precious Jade?” “How could I not?” replied Yucun. “Lately there has been much talk that he too has renounced the world and entered the religious life. I had dealings with him several times in those days, yet never imagined that he could make so absolute a break.” “That is not so,” said Shiyin. “I knew of this strange destiny before it unfolded. Years ago, before you and I spoke outside the gate of my old home in Renqing Lane, I had already met him once.” Yucun asked in astonishment, “The capital lies a great distance from your native place. How could you have met him?” “Our spirits had long been in communion,” replied Shiyin. Yucun said, “If that is so, you must surely know where Baoyu is now.” Shiyin replied, “Baoyu is indeed the Precious Jade. Before the Rong and Ning mansions were confiscated that year, on the day when Baochai and Daiyu were parted, the jade had already left the mortal world. It did so first to avert disaster and second to bring about a union. Once its predestined bonds were fulfilled, form and substance became one again; then, after displaying a little more of its divine power by winning the highest honors and begetting a noble son, it revealed itself as a treasure endowed with the rarest powers of Heaven and Earth, beyond comparison with anything mortal. Formerly the Great Luminary Vast-Expanse and the Immortal of Boundless Space brought it down to the mortal world. Now that its earthly destiny is fulfilled, those same two have carried it back to its original abode. That is what became of Baoyu.” Though Yucun could not understand it all, he grasped four or five parts in ten. Nodding, he sighed, “So that is how it was. In my ignorance, I knew nothing of it. But if Baoyu had such an origin, why did he become so deeply infatuated, only to awaken so completely afterward? I beg you to enlighten me further.” Shiyin smiled. “Even if I told you, you might not fully comprehend the matter. The Land of Illusion in the Great Void is itself the Blessed Realm of True Suchness. Having once examined the registers and seen the course of things from beginning to end, with every event of his life set out clearly before him, how could he fail to awaken? When the immortal herb returned to its true nature, how could the Stone of Spiritual Understanding not also be restored to its origin?” At this, Yucun ceased to understand him. Realizing that these were mysteries of the immortals, he thought it improper to press further and instead said, “I have now heard your teaching concerning Baoyu. But with so many young ladies in our clan, why did all of them, beginning with Imperial Consort Yuanchun, meet such ordinary ends?” Shiyin sighed. “Do not take offense at my clumsy words, sir, but all the daughters of your noble clan came from the Heaven of Passion and the Sea of Retribution. As a rule, women past and present must of course never transgress in lust; yet even passion itself is something they cannot touch without becoming tainted. Thus Cui Yingying and Su Xiaoxiao were merely immortals whose hearts turned toward the mortal world, while Song Yu and Sima Xiangru incurred grave sins of the tongue as men of letters. As for those entangled in lingering passion, one had better not ask how they end.”

p.src: One day, the Taoist Kongkong once again passed before Greensickness Peak. Seeing that the stone rejected for the repair of Heaven was still there and that the inscription upon it remained unchanged, he read it carefully once more from the beginning. After the concluding verses he found a lengthy account of how all the entanglements had been resolved, and nodded with a sigh. “When I first saw this strange tale of Brother Stone, I said it might become a marvel known throughout the world, and so I copied it down; but then I had not yet seen him return to his origin and regain his true nature. I did not know when this fine sequel had been added. Now I see that Brother Stone’s one descent into the mortal world polished him to radiance and brought him to perfect enlightenment; truly, he can be said to have no regret remaining. I fear only that, as the years pass, the writing will grow indistinct and errors creep in. I had better copy it out once more, find some idle person in the world with nothing to occupy him, and entrust him to spread it far and wide, so that people may understand how the marvelous is not marvelous, the commonplace not commonplace, the true not true, and the false not false. Or perhaps, when the dusty dream has wearied men, they may ask the birds to call them home; and perhaps the mountain spirits, being hospitable, may once more send something flying here transformed from stone. Who can say?” Having reached this decision, he copied it out again, tucked the manuscript into his sleeve, and returned to the bustling, prosperous world. He searched everywhere, but found only men bent on winning distinction and establishing careers or glib-tongued fellows struggling to earn their bread. Who among them had the leisure or inclination to chatter further about a stone? At last he searched as far as the Ford of the Rushing Torrent and the Ferry of Awakening from Delusion, where he found a man asleep inside a thatched hut. Thinking that this must surely be an idle fellow, he decided to show him the copy he had made of The Story of the Stone. But no matter how he called, the man would not wake. The Taoist Kongkong tugged at him with all his strength, and only then did the man slowly open his eyes and sit up. He gave the manuscript a cursory glance, tossed it down again, and said, “I witnessed all these events myself long ago and know the whole story. Your copy contains no serious errors. I need only direct you to one person and have you entrust it to him for circulation; that will bring this curious case to its conclusion.” The Taoist Kongkong hurriedly asked who this person was. The man replied, “On a certain day of a certain month in a certain year, you must go to a place called the Studio for Mourning the Red. There you will find a Mr. Cao Xueqin. Simply tell him that these are words from Jia Yucun and ask him to do thus and so.” With that, he lay down and went back to sleep.

p.src: The Taoist Kongkong committed these words firmly to memory. Who knows how many ages and kalpas passed thereafter, but at last there really was a Studio for Mourning the Red, where he found Mr. Cao Xueqin leafing through the histories of bygone times. The Taoist Kongkong delivered Jia Yucun’s message, then showed him The Story of the Stone. Mr. Xueqin laughed. “So these really are ‘false words and rustic speech’!” The Taoist Kongkong asked, “How is it, sir, that you know this man and are willing to pass on his story?” Mr. Cao Xueqin laughed. “They call you ‘Empty,’ and indeed your belly is utterly empty. Since it is only ‘false words and rustic speech,’ so long as it contains no scribal errors, absurdities, or contradictions, I shall gladly share it with two or three like-minded friends after wine and a full meal, or beneath the lamplit window on a rainy evening, to while away our loneliness. There is no need for eminent gentlemen to judge it and make it famous. To probe its roots and demand its foundations as you do is like marking the gunwale to recover a lost sword, or gluing the tuning pegs before playing a zither.” Hearing this, the Taoist Kongkong threw back his head and laughed. He cast down the manuscript and drifted away. As he walked, he said aloud, “It truly is a contrived absurdity!
